docs.text: VCS PySTAC extension ¶ pystac-ext-vcs provides VcsExtension for version-control references on PySTAC Catalogs, Collections, Items, Assets, and Links. The wrapper targets the VCS v0.1.0 schema . Its four optional fields describe the version-control system, branch, exact revision, and release tag. System names are open strings, so Git, Subversion, and other systems are supported. python -m pip install pystac-ext-vcs Record a source revision . Update fields, assets, links, and templates . Look up VCS fields . Browse the Python API . Understand architecture and validation .

docs.text: Scope, architecture, and validation ¶ Package structure ¶ The distribution is pystac-ext-vcs ; import the wrapper from pystac.extensions.vcs . The wheel excludes the shared namespace initializer owned by PySTAC. VcsExtension uses PySTAC's PropertiesExtension and ExtensionManagementMixin . It wraps existing metadata dictionaries in place, preserving normal PySTAC serialization and cloning. No separate schema model or generated data class is needed. The authoritative contract remains the published VCS v0.1.0 JSON Schema . VCS_EXTENSION_HOOKS identifies the schema and the Catalog, Collection, and Item object types. There are no previous extension identifiers. The package does not automatically register migration hooks or an .ext.vcs accessor. Validation boundaries ¶ Property assignments, apply() , and serialization do not run JSON Schema validation. apply() updates fields sequentially and clears omitted values. It does not create repository links or resolve branches and tags. Install pystac[validation] and call the owning STAC object's validate() to check the complete document. Schema retrieval may require network access or an application-configured schema cache. Tests cache the unmodified published extension schema locally and validate its contract without network access. The schema permits absent fields but rejects nulls, empty strings, non-string values, and unknown vcs: keys in its defined field locations. The prose specification additionally asks for at least one field; see the field reference .

docs.text: Install and build ¶ Install the library ¶ The package declares Python 3.10 or later and PySTAC >=1,<2 . The test matrix covers Python 3.10–3.14. python -m pip install pystac-ext-vcs python -c "from pystac.extensions.vcs import VcsExtension; print(VcsExtension.get_schema_uri())" Install from a checkout ¶ git clone https://github.com/Terradue/pystac-ext-vcs.git cd pystac-ext-vcs python -m pip install -e . If an existing editable installation predates a packaging change, repeat the editable install in that environment. Preview the documentation ¶ Install the package and documentation tools in the same environment. Use a regular install for documentation: static API discovery does not reliably find editable modules inside the shared PySTAC namespace. Reinstall after changing source code: python -m pip install . "mkdocs<2" mkdocs-material "mkdocstrings[python]" mkdocs serve Build with warnings treated as errors: mkdocs build --strict Run repository checks ¶ With Hatch installed, run these commands from the checkout: hatch run dev:check hatch run dev:typecheck hatch run dev:security hatch run test:test

docs.text: Work with VCS metadata ¶ Update and clear fields ¶ Continue from the tutorial : vcs = VcsExtension . ext ( catalog ) vcs . branch = "develop" vcs . tag = None assert "vcs:tag" not in catalog . extra_fields vcs . apply ( vcs_type = "svn" , revision = "1234" ) assert vcs . branch is None Missing fields return None ; assigning None removes the field. apply() replaces all four fields, clearing any omitted arguments. Other metadata is preserved. Declare the extension ¶ VcsExtension.ext(target) checks the schema declaration. Pass add_if_missing=True to add it to a Catalog, Collection, or Item, or to the owner of an Asset or Link. Repeated calls do not duplicate the declaration. Use VcsExtension.add_to(stac_object) , has_extension(stac_object) , and remove_from(stac_object) to manage declarations directly. Removing a declaration does not delete stored fields. Attach Assets and Links ¶ import pystac from pystac.extensions.vcs import VcsExtension collection = pystac . Collection ( "software" , "Source code" , pystac . Extent ( pystac . SpatialExtent ([[ - 180 , - 90 , 180 , 90 ]]), pystac . TemporalExtent ([[ None , None ]]), ), ) asset = pystac . Asset ( "https://example.org/source.zip" ) collection . add_asset ( "source" , asset ) VcsExtension . ext ( asset , add_if_missing = True ) . apply ( vcs_type = "git" , tag = "v1.0" ) link = pystac . Link ( "vcs" , "https://example.org/repository" ) collection . add_link ( link ) VcsExtension . ext ( link ) . revision = "abc123" Attach the Asset or Link before using add_if_missing=True . An unowned Asset or Link can be wrapped with the default False , but its eventual owner must declare the extension. Values on owners are never inherited. Link templates ¶ PySTAC stores linkTemplates as extra fields. Build a template with a standalone Link, then serialize it into the owning object's template list: template = pystac . Link ( "vcs" , "https://example.org/ {repository} " ) VcsExtension . ext ( template ) . apply ( vcs_type = "git" , branch = "main" ) VcsExtension . add_to ( collection ) collection . extra_fields [ "linkTemplates" ] = [ template . to_dict ()] This assignment replaces the template list. To edit an existing template, load its dictionary with pystac.Link.from_dict() , edit it using VcsExtension.ext() , and write to_dict() back to the list. There is no dedicated summaries, item-asset-definition, or asset-template helper in this implementation; it covers the field locations explicitly constrained by the v0.1.0 JSON Schema.

docs.text: VCS fields ¶ JSON field Python property Meaning vcs:type vcs_type Version-control system, e.g. git , svn , or a custom name. vcs:branch branch Line of development, e.g. main . vcs:revision revision Exact revision, e.g. a commit hash or changelist. vcs:tag tag Release marker, e.g. v1.0.0 . All four fields are optional nonempty strings in the v0.1.0 schema . Unknown vcs: fields are rejected; unrelated metadata is permitted. System names are not an enum. The schema applies these constraints to Catalogs, Collections, Item properties, Assets, Links, and linkTemplates . Getters return None for missing fields; setters accept None to remove fields. Setters and apply() do not perform schema validation. Empty strings can be stored but fail subsequent validation. The versioned specification asks for at least one VCS field where the extension is used. The published JSON Schema does not enforce that requirement. Set at least one field for a meaningful reference.

docs.text: Record a source revision ¶ Install the package , then run this example: import pystac from pystac.extensions.vcs import VcsExtension catalog = pystac . Catalog ( "source" , "Source-controlled catalog" ) vcs = VcsExtension . ext ( catalog , add_if_missing = True ) vcs . apply ( vcs_type = "git" , branch = "main" , revision = "abc123" , tag = "v1.0.0" ) source = pystac . Link ( "vcs" , "https://example.org/team/repository" ) catalog . add_link ( source ) VcsExtension . ext ( source ) . apply ( vcs_type = "git" , revision = "abc123" ) serialized = catalog . to_dict () assert serialized [ "vcs:branch" ] == "main" assert VcsExtension . get_schema_uri () in serialized [ "stac_extensions" ] restored = pystac . Catalog . from_dict ( serialized ) assert VcsExtension . ext ( restored ) . revision == "abc123" Collections use the same top-level fields; Items store VCS metadata in properties . Links and Assets store their own fields and do not inherit their owner's values. Use VcsExtension.ext(target) explicitly; no target.ext.vcs shortcut is registered. Serialization does not perform validation. See validation boundaries .
